children: Chakrabarty brings over two decades of cross-industry HR experience to Isgec, with a mandate spanning people strategy, talent and organisational development

Mahua Chakrabarty has been appointed Chief Human Resources Officer at Isgec Heavy Engineering, effective 1 October 2026. She joins the company’s senior management team with more than two decades of experience across engineering, manufacturing, technology, financial services and consulting.

Before joining Isgec, Chakrabarty served as Regional Head – HR, ISEAP (India, Southeast Asia and Pacific) at Maccaferri, where she led the people portfolio across the region and was part of the regional leadership team. Her remit included aligning people strategy with business priorities across multiple markets.

Earlier, she was Group CHRO – India, Middle East and Africa at SEMAC Consultants, part of the Dalmia Group, where she handled HR across the regions with responsibilities spanning organisational alignment, productivity, mergers and acquisitions and cultural integration.

Her previous leadership roles also include Senior Director – HR & Training at Xebia, covering India, the Middle East and the US, and Director – Human Resources & Training at Hilti, where she spent nearly a decade. Earlier in her career, she held HR and training roles at Quipo Infrastructure and GE Capital.

Across these roles, Chakrabarty has built experience in people strategy, talent management, organisational development, culture building, leadership coaching, industrial relations and change management. Her LinkedIn profile also lists certifications in executive coaching, psychometric assessment, Six Sigma and FranklinCovey leadership training.

Chakrabarty holds a Diploma in Business Management with specialisation in Human Resources and Marketing and has completed a leadership and management programme at IMD Business School, Lausanne. At Isgec, she will oversee the company’s people strategy, talent management, organisational development, change management and HR operations as it continues to expand its engineering and manufacturing businesses.
